title: The merkaba — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
The merkaba — 8 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the ring. 8 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 4 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 24 pair(s); the theorems fall into 3 strand(s), the largest of 6. Most binding: tetA (5), tetB (5), dbl (3), axis (2). 1 theorem(s) name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: z9.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 file(s): src/proof/merkaba.lean, src/proof/z9.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to 4d1e4226-de62-81f2-9e4e-1f28aad0eb1d. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (7, 7, 3, 6, 1, 6, 6). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: address.lean (5 observed, 1.51 expected, lift 3.31), light.lean (3 observed, 1.15 expected, lift 2.6), elementary.lean (5 observed, 2.84 expected, lift 1.76). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.11; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.47. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 49.5% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. the partition into {3,6,9} and two three-element classes closed under doubling is the subgroup and coset structure of Z/9 under the action of U(9); Lagrange. One theorem already credits Euler for the polyhedron formula. Searched 2026-09-04; prior art found and credited Credited per theorem: the_cube_and_the_tetrahedron_count_out — Euler's polyhedron formula V − E + F = 2 (Leonhard Euler, 1758). The file as a whole is this deposit's own construction, and this ONE declaration restates a named classical result: its third conjunct 4 + 4 - 6 = 2 IS the Euler characteristic of the tetrahedron. The comment above that theorem already named Euler; the register did not, because prior art was routed on the FILE and a file-level row cannot say "own work except theorem 7". No priority over Euler is claimed. What is this deposit's own here is the pairing of the two tetrahedra with the cube Q₃ and the vertex and edge counts around it, not the characteristic.. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. the_three_classes_partition_z9 — axis.length = 3 ∧ tetA.length = 3 ∧ tetB.length = 3 ∧ (axis ++ tetA ++ tetB).eraseDups.length = 9 ∧ ((List.range 9).all (fun d => (axis ++ tetA ++ tetB).contains d)) record
  2. the_axis_is_closed_under_doubling — (dbl axis).all (fun d => axis.contains d) record
  3. doubling_counter_rotates_the_two_tetrahedra — (dbl tetA).eraseDups.length = 3 ∧ (dbl tetA).all (fun d => tetB.contains d) ∧ (dbl tetB).eraseDups.length = 3 ∧ (dbl tetB).all (fun d => tetA.contains d) record
  4. the_counter_rotation_has_period_two — (dbl (dbl tetA)).all (fun d => tetA.contains d) ∧ (dbl (dbl tetB)).all (fun d => tetB.contains d) record
  5. the_tetrahedra_residue_sums_cancel — m9 (tetA.foldl (· + ·) 0) = 3 ∧ m9 (tetB.foldl (· + ·) 0) = 6 ∧ m9 (tetA.foldl (· + ·) 0 + tetB.foldl (· + ·) 0) = 0 record
  6. one_tetrahedron_covers_half_the_units — (units.filter (fun d => tetA.contains d)).length = 3 ∧ (units.filter (fun d => tetB.contains d)).length = 3 ∧ units.length = 6 record
  7. the_cube_and_the_tetrahedron_count_out — 2 ^ 3 = 8 ∧ 3 * 2 ^ 2 = 12 ∧ 4 + 4 - 6 = 2 record
  8. stacked_triangles_are_tetrahedral — (List.range' 1 40).all (fun n => sumTri n == n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) / 6) record
